name: Commission proposal
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the European Chemicals Agency and amending Regulations (EC) No 1907/2006, (EU) No 528/2012, (EU) No 649/2012 and (EU) 2019/1021
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to strengthen the European Chemicals Agency, the European Union body that checks whether chemicals are safe. Members propose giving it clearer duties, more say in how it is funded, and stronger rules against conflicts of interest. They also want it to work more closely with other European Union agencies on health and environment. Parliament can ask the agency for scientific opinions, and so can member states. The agency would also get a reserve fund to cope with uneven income from industry fees.

- **What changes:** the agency gets new tasks, a reserve fund and closer ties with other European Union agencies.
- **Who it affects:** the chemicals agency, national authorities, industry, workers and citizens exposed to chemicals.
- **What happens next:** Parliament adopted its position; talks with member states follow before the law is final.
